Area.evidence_source: The participants felt broken, guilty and full of shame after the violence happened which concurs with a population study of trauma-related shame and guilt after violence and sexual abuse (30). Suicidal thoughts seemed to be a normal part of the life of the participants that they had to struggle with after the sexual violence. Much stress and strain increased suicidal thoughts in the men, and societal discourse about sexual violence in the community, even if important, became a source of stress. It is important to note the relationship between planning a suicide and stopping at a critical moment. David talked about feeling calmer as he organised his suicide in more detail. Symptoms of imminent suicidal attempts are, for example, calmness (32).
